claims.text: The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is an as-solidified, single-phase solid solution.
The dynamic strength–ductility balance of Co-free FeNiCrMn is governed by a temperature- and strain-rate-dependent transition between dislocation glide and deformation twinning.
Removing Co from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi increases the stacking-fault energy.
At lower temperatures and high strain rates, deformation twinning is activated in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Twinning under low-temperature, high-strain-rate conditions compensates for reduced dislocation mobility.
Activation of deformation twinning sustains strain hardening and ductility.
Deformation twins act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Twin-mediated obstruction of dislocation motion increases the strain-hardening rate.
Twin-induced strain hardening offsets a potential loss of ductility caused by the absence of Co.
At higher temperatures and lower strain rates, Co-free FeNiCrMn deforms primarily by dislocation glide.
Under low-temperature, high-strain-rate conditions, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have a higher deformation-twin density than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Under low-temperature, high-strain-rate conditions, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have a higher strain-hardening rate than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Under high-temperature, low-strain-rate conditions, Co-free FeNiCrMn and equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi will both deform primarily by dislocation glide.
Under high-temperature, low-strain-rate conditions, Co-free FeNiCrMn and equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi will show similar mechanical responses.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi is expected to exhibit dominant dislocation glide and a lower incidence of twinning than Co-free FeNiCrMn under comparable low-temperature, high-strain-rate conditions.
The proposed twinning mechanism is limited to sufficiently low temperatures and high strain rates and should be insignificant at high temperatures and low strain rates.
